h: וַיֵּלֶךְ וְשַׁבָּת תְּשׁוּבָה, י״ב Vayeilech and Shabbos Shuvah, 12

p: for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory."
a person can reach up to the Throne of Glory;
even if he increased his sins
up to the Throne of Glory,
The Pesikta d'Rav Kahana (24:12) as well
The concept of the Throne of Glory
that is at the utmost perfection,
"He grasps the face of the Throne"
And the Pesikta mentioned above says
"Great is teshuvah, for it reaches," etc.,
וְלֹא תֹאמַר עַד לָרָקִיעַ רִאשׁוֹן וְכוּלֵּי,
"and do not say up to the first heaven," etc.,
"nor up to the second heaven," etc.,
"but up to the Throne of Glory;
כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמַר דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
'My sins have passed over my head'
'Our sins have multiplied above our head,
and our guilt has grown up to the heavens'
This accords with Rabbeinu Chananel's explanation.
This level no one could attain
for in the place where baalei teshuvah stand
for they draw close to HaKadosh Baruch Hu,
which is the intellect hidden from all thought.
Likewise, even one who blemished the root,
who increased his sins up to the Throne of Glory,
גַּם כֵּן יָכוֹל לְתַקֵּן עַל יְדֵי תְשׁוּבָה.
can also rectify it through teshuvah.
For it is stated in the holy Zohar
that the nefesh, ruach and neshamah in a person
The nefesh is from Asiyah, the world of the Ofanim,
and there it is mostly evil;
the ruach is from Yetzirah, the world of the angels,
and there it is half good and half evil.
The dwelling place of the ruach is in the heart,
and there are the two chambers of the heart:
"A wise man's heart is at his right,
and a fool's heart at his left"
and there dwell the two angels
the yetzer tov and the yetzer hara.
And the neshamah is from Beriah,
and there it is entirely good,
as it is stated in the holy Zohar
(תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר פב, ב; זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג קט, ב):
"Souls that are hewn from the Throne" —
"The soul You placed within me is pure."
And from the aspect of the neshamah it is
for as soon as he is circumcised at eight days
since at that point he does not yet have
rather Hashem Yisbarach draws him near from His side,
"And He blew into his nostrils the breath of life"
and it is stated in the Tikkunei Zohar:
"One who blows, blows from within himself."
But at the time of sin
the aspect of neshamah departs from him.
וְיֵשׁ אֲשֶׁר מַגְדִּיל חֶטְאוֹ כָּל כָּךְ
And there is one who increases his sin so much
that he is uprooted entirely from the root,
because they are attached to the root.
וְאֵלּוּ שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם חֵלֶק לָעוֹלָם הַבָּא
And "these have no share in Olam Haba"
implies that it is because they separated entirely,
having sinned up to the root,
as it is stated in Tanna d'Vei Eliyahu
For "I am" is a positive mitzvah,
yet it is not a command
that you should know that I am Hashem your G-d;
rather it is stated as a certainty —
meaning that we are rooted in the root
and Michah blemished the root itself.
This is the pasuk of Ezra
that the Pesikta mentioned above brings,
where he said: "For our sins have multiplied
And this is what the Gemara says:
for it reaches up to the Throne of Glory" —
that even if the sins reach
up to the Throne of Glory,
This is as stated in the Ramban, z"l,
that it refers to the teshuvah mentioned before;
that it refers to the entire Torah.
But according to this it should have written
and since it is written "this mitzvah,"
that it refers to what is written
which is the matter of teshuvah.
He cites the pasuk at the start of the parashah there:
"And you will take it to your heart"
"and you will return unto Hashem your G-d," etc.
that this is the mitzvah of teshuvah;
and that concerning this it concludes:
"For it is very near to you," etc.
"in your mouth" — this is verbal confession;
"and in your heart" — this is regret in the heart
"to do it" — this is the resolution for the future
to act according to the will of Hashem Yisbarach.
(According to his words it is well understood
why it does not say "and in your deeds":
דְּזֶה לֹא קָאֵי עַל הַמַּעֲשֶׂה בְּפוֹעַל
for this does not refer to the actual deed,
as "in your mouth and in your heart" are actual,
but to the resolution in the heart to act.)
Now, according to the Ramban's explanation, z"l,
that it refers to the mitzvah of teshuvah,
we must understand what connection there is
in its writing "It is not in heaven"
that it refers to the Torah,
"it is not in heaven" is understandable,
(דְּבָרִים רַבָּה ח, ו; בָּבָא מְצִיעָא נט, ב)
שֶׁמִּן הַתּוֹרָה לֹא נִשְׁאַר כְּלוּם בַּשָּׁמַיִם,
that nothing of the Torah remained in heaven;
rather it was entirely handed over to Yisrael.
But if it refers to teshuvah,
and "Nor is it beyond the sea"
to the two aspects of teshuvah.
"And you will take it to your heart
where Hashem your G-d has dispersed you";
that reaches up to the Throne of Glory
that even if the sins reach
up to the Throne of Glory —
as it is written: "among all the nations
For the yetzer hara and subjugation to the kingdoms
and this is why it says
"among all the nations where He has dispersed you":
that even if he blemished through his sin
by way of all the kelipos in the world,
that is, up to the root,
אַף עַל פִּי כֵן יוֹעִיל לְךָ הַתְּשׁוּבָה
for it too reaches up to the root.
"And you will return unto Hashem your G-d" —
alluding that through teshuvah he draws near
up to the Throne of Glory,
in the place where baalei teshuvah stand
for they draw close to the root of holiness,
which is the intellect hidden from all thought.
Concerning this it is written afterwards:
nifleis is related to pele, wonder,
which is the intellect hidden from all thought;
up to the Throne of Glory,
to the intellect hidden from all thought.
alludes that even if he increased sins
up to the Throne of Glory,
so that he became entirely distant even from the root,
that brings him close to the holiness of the root,
This is the meaning of "It is not in heaven":
"Who will go up to heaven for us"
and the perception of such a light —
for he can draw near even to heaven,
that is, to the holiness of the Throne of Glory,
alludes to the increase of sins
up to the Throne of Glory;
which are likened to the sea.
in the heart of Bnei Yisrael derives,
"Like the roaring of the seas they roar"
the gathering of all seventy nations;
and likewise, ensnared in the kelipos
Therefore it is called "beyond the sea":
all the seventy nations became distant,
"like the roaring of the seas they roar."
This is why it says "Nor is it far off":
lest you think it is too far to reach —
and who is it that can cross
and conquer such a great immersion,
to bring this into the depths of our hearts?
וְעַל זֶה אָמַר כִּי אֵינוֹ כֵן:
On this it says that it is not so:
כִּי עַל יְדֵי הִשְׁתַּדְּלוּת מוּעָט שֶׁלּוֹ,
to come unto Hashem your G-d.
עַל פָּסוּק פִּתְחִי לִי אֲחוֹתִי וְכוּלֵּי
on the pasuk "Open for Me, My sister," etc.
"Open for Me an opening of teshuvah
like the point of a needle,
and I will open great openings," etc.;
"Who opens the gate to those who knock in teshuvah" —
and asks, and yearns to return,
Hashem Yisbarach opens the gate to teshuvah.
